composers_checked.name: Boccherini, Luigi
composers_checked.note: Quintets G. 265-402 and sextets G. 454-459 checked against the Wikipedia list (after Gérard) and the Quebec Gérard catalogue; floor and minutes from Apple Music track lists (iTunes API), MusicBrainz and the Karski Quartet Vol. 2 track list. Gap check added Op. 27, Op. 29 and Op. 62 Nos. 1 and 5 (not on IMSLP).

note: Boccherini string quintets and sextets: complete. Kept every quintet with a commercial recording found: Opp. 10-31 complete (La Magnifica Comunità and I Virtuosi della Rotonda cycles, Brilliant Classics, plus Europa Galante, Ensemble 415, Vanbrugh, Smithsonian, Ensemble Explorations), Op. 36 No. 6, Op. 39, Op. 40 Nos. 1-2, Op. 41, Op. 42, Op. 43 No. 2, Op. 45 Nos. 1 and 4, Op. 46 Nos. 3-4, Op. 51, Op. 60 (all but the lost No. 4; Elisa Baciocchi Quintet, Da Vinci 2024), Op. 62 Nos. 1 and 5, and the six sextets Op. 23. Gap check (not on IMSLP): Op. 27 (six quintettini, La Magnifica Comunità Vol. VII), Op. 29 (I Virtuosi della Rotonda Vol. X) and Op. 62 Nos. 1 and 5; Op. 62 Nos. 2, 3, 4 and 6 (G. 398-400, 402) have no recording found and are not added. Not recorded, skipped: Op. 36 Nos. 1-5, Op. 40 Nos. 3-6, Op. 43 Nos. 1 and 3, Op. 45 Nos. 2-3, Op. 46 Nos. 1, 2, 5, 6, Op. 49, Op. 50. IMSLP's "Unrecorded" notes on its synthesized files are out of date (the 2023-26 Karski Quartet and Elisa Baciocchi discs record several), so the late sets are worth re-checking in a year or two. Keys follow Gérard (Wikipedia list, Quebec catalogue): the IMSLP Op. 10 page lists G. 269 as A major and G. 270 as C major, Gérard has E-flat and D. G. 396 is F major (Wikipedia says E). Op. 39 is for double bass with a cello alternative (first edition); Op. 51 is kept with two cellos (IMSLP: a viola may replace cello 1). Not added: G. 379-390 (two-viola versions of the piano quintets) and G. 403-405 (two-viola arrangements by an unknown hand), no recordings; G. 460 is by Brunetti. Levels: one estimate per opus group (4 for Opp. 10-39 and the sextets, 5 for Opp. 40-62), anchored on Op. 11 No. 5 (4); hardest part "violin 1" as in the benchmark, though cello 1 is often as hard. Stabat Mater question (outOfScope, c28 territory): the 1781 version is for soprano and string quintet one to a part (Sarasa Ensemble, Naxos 2019), so the census reason "string orchestra" is wrong for it; whether a sacred work counts as chamber music is for the owner.
